Welcome to **docs**! This site is built with [Astro](https://astro.build/) and the
[Starlight](https://starlight.astro.build/) documentation theme.

## Run locally

```bash
pnpm nx start @agentic-sdlc/docs
```

## Build for production

```bash
pnpm nx build @agentic-sdlc/docs
```

## Adding a locale

Add an entry to the `locales` block in `astro.config.mjs` and create a matching
directory under `src/content/docs/<locale>/`. Starlight will pick up the new locale
automatically.

## Locale-aware links

Use the generated `Link` component whenever you want to link to another page
**inside** your docs — it automatically resolves the current locale, so a single
source of truth produces the right URL in every language:

```mdx
import Link from '@components/link.astro';

<Link path="guides/getting-started">Read the getting-started guide</Link>
```

Here is the component in action: <Link path="guides/getting-started">back to this page</Link>.

For regular external links, just use ordinary Markdown `[label](url)`.

## The sample app

This repo includes a small notes app, scaffolded with the Nx Plugin for AWS generators, to
give the lifecycle something real to act on:

| Project | Generator | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `packages/notes-table` | `ts#dynamodb` | ElectroDB `note` entity, local DynamoDB for dev |
| `packages/notes-api` | `ts#trpc-api` | tRPC procedures: list, create, update, delete notes |
| `packages/notes-website` | `ts#react-website` | React + Vite + TanStack Router + shadcn/ui |

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev   # DynamoDB local (Docker), API and website
```

No infrastructure (CDK) is generated; the app runs locally only.
What this repository documents and how it relates to Discava.

This repository illustrates the **Agentic SDLC** adopted in
[Discava](https://github.com/AlexTo/discava), a serverless, AWS-native Learning
Management System built with AI agents from the start.

It documents the practices, not the product: how work is specified, handed to agents,
verified and shipped.

## The loop at a glance

```d2
direction: right
spec: Spec\n(spec, plan, tasks)
review: Human review
issue: Implementation issue
agent: Agent opens PR
ci: CI checks
merge: Merge to main
deploy: Deploy

spec -> review: spec PR
review -> issue: merged + labelled spec-ready
issue -> agent
agent -> ci
ci -> agent: failure (max 3 retries)
ci -> merge: pass + human review
merge -> issue: next task
merge -> deploy
```

How failing checks send the agent back to fix its work.

When the PR Checks workflow fails on an agent's branch, the **Agent CI Status** workflow posts a
failure commit status that the automation reads, sending the agent back to revise the same pull
request in its original conversation.

- At most **three** fix attempts per PR, tracked with `ci-fix-1` to `ci-fix-3` labels.
- After that the workflow comments and stops (`ci-fix-exhausted`) and a human takes over.
- A passing run posts nothing.

Bounding retries keeps cost predictable and makes sure a stuck agent escalates to a person.
How merged specs become agent-authored pull requests.

1. A merged spec PR labelled `spec-ready` triggers the **Agent Issues** workflow, which opens
   the first implementation issue from `tasks.md`.
2. An implementing agent polls for issues carrying its label and opens a pull request from a
   dedicated branch prefix.
3. The agent's PR ticks the completed tasks in `tasks.md`.
4. When that PR merges, the workflow opens the **next** issue, repeating until the task list is done.

Only the agent's own branches advance the chain; other merged PRs are ignored so the process
cannot loop on its own edits.
How work is defined before an agent touches code.

Each feature starts as a folder under `specs/`, created with [Spec Kit](https://github.com/github/spec-kit)
skills (`specify`, `clarify`, `plan`, `tasks`, `analyze`). A spec folder contains:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `spec.md` | What and why: user stories, requirements, acceptance criteria |
| `plan.md` | How: technical approach and design decisions |
| `research.md`, `data-model.md`, `contracts/` | Supporting design detail |
| `tasks.md` | Ordered, checkable implementation tasks |
| `checklists/` | Requirement-quality checklists |

Folders are timestamp-numbered (e.g. `20261115-204447-certificates`).

The spec lands via a normal pull request. A human reviews it, and labelling it `spec-ready`
before merge is the signal to start implementation.
